transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because most days I just feel really low… like I’m stuck at the bottom of some dark hole. Even when I’m around people I know, I still can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling.
How long have you been feeling this low?
About a year and two months now. It really started after that fall at the HVAC job, when I hurt my back… after that, things just started unraveling.
Since this started, have you felt this low most days without a break for two months or more?
Yes. It’s been pretty much most days, without any real break, for about a year and two months now—since I fell at the HVAC job and hurt my back. Everything kind of started falling apart after that.
If your back injury and the problems that followed were suddenly resolved, do you think you would still feel this depressed?

I don’t know… I think it would help, sure, but this feels bigger than just my back. Most days I still feel like I’m at the bottom of a dark hole, and even around people I know, that heavy, hopeless feeling doesn’t really lift.
Before this current stretch began, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had hard times before, but I don’t remember feeling like this for a solid couple weeks the way it’s been this time.
When your mind is not on your back injury or the problems that came after it, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah… even when I’m not thinking about my back or all the mess that came after, I still feel depressed. It’s like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole most days. Even if I’m around people I know, that heavy, hopeless feeling is still there.
Do you often feel anxious or worried, even when nothing specific is happening?
I’m not really sure. I do worry some, but I haven’t noticed it happening for no reason all the time. It’s hard for me to separate from everything else.
Before this began, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been down before, but I can’t really remember a time before this where it was nearly every day for two weeks like you’re asking.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes. I used to really enjoy hiking, painting, going to the makerspace and tinkering with things… even figuring out a tricky install at work. Now I’ll just stare at the supplies or not answer when people call. None of it feels worth starting.
Have you had trouble sleeping?
Yes. Some nights I’m just lying there for hours, my back hurting and bills running through my head. Other times I sleep half the day, but I still wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yeah, it’s changed. My eating is kind of all over the place. I’ll go most of the day just drinking coffee because food makes my stomach turn, and then late at night I’ll pick at whatever’s in the cabinet, but I’m not really hungry or tasting it.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Yes… I have. I’ve had thoughts like maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes when the pain and the money stuff all piles up, I catch myself thinking about ending it. It scares me, but the thoughts are there.
Have you been feeling worthless or like everything is your fault?

Yeah. I keep telling myself I’m useless now, like because I can’t work the way I used to, I’m just… no good. And I go over everything in my head—apprentices I feel like I let down, bills I haven’t paid. It all feels like proof that I messed everything up.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for several days in a row?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I get irritable sometimes, but I haven’t had days where I felt high or full of energy like that.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. It’s been really hard to focus. Paperwork and repair diagrams I used to understand right away just kind of blur together now. I’ll sit there stuck, not even able to decide something simple like which form to open first.
Do these feelings seem much stronger than you would expect from the problems that started after your back injury?

Yes… I think they are. I know the back injury caused real problems, but the way I talk to myself feels bigger than that. I keep thinking I’m useless because I can’t work like I used to, and I replay every apprentice I let down and every unpaid bill like it proves I ruined everything.
If the financial and work problems from your injury were gone, would you still feel this depressed?

Yes. I think I would. The money and work stuff make it worse, but even when I’m not thinking about that, most days I feel like I’m at the bottom of a dark hole. Even around people I know, there’s this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t shake.
Do you still feel depressed even at times when your back pain, money problems, and work situation are not on your mind?

Yes. Even when I’m not thinking about my back or the bills or work, it’s still there. Most days it feels like I’m at the bottom of a dark hole, and even if I’m around people I know, I can’t shake that heavy, hopeless feeling.
Has this depressed mood lasted for two years or more?
No, not two years. It’s been about a year and two months, since I fell on that HVAC job and hurt my back, and everything started unraveling after that.
